title: Climbing Stairs
kidExplanation: A staircase. You can climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. How many different hop patterns reach the top?
plainProblem: Climbing Stairs: A staircase. Worked example — input: n = 2; expected output: 2. Why: 1+1 or 2. Interview pattern to name out loud: 1-D dynamic programming.

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Climbing Stairs”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input n = 2 should still produce 2.

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: See code.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To climb to the n-th stair, you have two options, 1. You can climb from the (n-1)-th stair. 2. You can climb from the (n-2)-th stair. So, the number of ways to reach the n-th stair is the sum of the number of ways to reach the (n-1)-th and (n-2)-th stairs. This forms a Fibonacci sequence where f(n) = f(n-1) + f(n-2).

thinkingSteps.title: Better idea
thinkingSteps.body: Commit to 1-D dynamic programming. Answer depends on smaller answers along one line. Walk example `n = 2` → `2` while naming each variable, then code. Close with See code time and O(1) space.
